To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fascial system is a complex, adaptable and resilient structure that can be manipulated by manual therapy.
fasciae are a continuous three-dimensional network, that they have a plastic and adaptive nature, and that they can be influenced by manipulative therapy.

(1) fascial tissue is a dynamic and adaptable system; (2) the fascial tissue is not a layer but a polyhedral continuum; (3) fascial microvacuoles have a plasticity based on a functional chaos; (4) the fascial continuum can be manipulated in order to restore its functional chaos.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the fascial continuum, which we define as an integrated and interconnected network of microvacuoles, which are the functional unit of fascial tissue, and which can be considered as a functional chaos, in which there is no predetermined logic.
the study of this phenomenon, and with the possibility of using this concept to improve the quality of the clinical practice.
the indeterminable resilience and adaptability of the fascial continuum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fascial system is the body system that has the highest level of plasticity and adaptability to the changing conditions, but this adaptability can be lost, and this is the cause of the onset of many diseases.

the fascial system is a continuum of polyhedral microstructures of connective tissue that, by hosting different specialized cells and by being in constant motion and tension, ensures the maintenance of the functional efficiency of the body system.

the fascial system is a complex and highly adaptive system, which, in response to the external stimuli, changes its shape and behavior, and is capable of maintaining the body systems in a state of optimal efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fascial microvacuoles, in response to internal and external stimuli, change shape, and this plasticity allows the body to adapt to changing conditions.

the fascia is a system of connective tissue microvacuoles, which are not fascial planes, and which, through the interaction of the different cell types and of the connective fibrils, form a dynamic and adaptable continuum.

the fascial continuum is the “fascial flock” that flies in a chaotic way, but always in a functional and efficient way, and that the therapist must learn how to fly with the flock, without trying to change its behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fascia is an adaptable continuum that can be influenced by the manipulative therapist.
fascia has an inherent ability to adapt to the changing internal conditions of the cell and to external forces.
the fascial tissue is a complex system that is not easy to study, but that is essential to understand the mechanisms of disease and to provide a rational therapeutic approach.
